final_comment: The CM550 1-D table lookup. Its one stack argument is a 14-byte table_lookup_1d_arguments_t: x_axis_offset (the byte offset of the point the previous lookup found; the search starts there and the new offset is written back), x_axis_pointer (byte count word then the points), x_input, y_values_pointer (the value of the point at byte offset n is at y_values_pointer + n) and no_interpolation_flag. It compares the input (unsigned) with the cached point first: below it, it clamps to the first point or searches down; at or above it, it clamps to the last point or searches up. Below the first point it returns the first value, at or above the last point the last value, and otherwise the value at the point at or below the input, linearly interpolated toward the next value (unsigned mulu / divu, one path per slope sign) unless no_interpolation_flag is nonzero. Counterpart of CM848's lookupTableInterpolation (0x55ef4: five register arguments, signed / unsigned / step flags, end points checked before the cache, one signed interpolation). (was lookupTableInterpolation; PR #53 round 95)
